summary: Rate-limiter epoch sawtooth pattern causing periodic 429 surges during scheduled warmup
description:
Issue summary:
Customer (Nimbus Labs, dedicated pool) reports recurring, periodic 429 throttles during their nightly scheduled warmup/scale-up job. Throttles appear as a sawtooth pattern: a sharp spike of 429s every ~20-25 seconds for a short window (10–15s), then recovery. This repeats for the duration of the warmup sequence.

Impact:
- Customer background warmup job stalls intermittently (throughput drops by ~35% during spikes).
- Latency-sensitive inference calls receive 429s, causing internal retry waves and client-side cascading backoff.
- Affects production inference in us-east-1 for Nimbus dedicated pool; customer reports increased error rates for 45 minutes each night during warmup.

Environment:
- Customer-tier: dedicated GPU pool (reserved capacity).
- Region: prod us-east-1.
- API path: /v1/chat/streaming and /v1/embeddings/batch during warmup.
- Observed on both HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 ingress.

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Schedule concurrent warmup clients (20 short-run workers) to hit warmup route every 50ms for 5 minutes.
2) Observe global tenant token usage and rate-limit headers.
3) Notice periodic 429 bursts aligned with warmup start + autoscaler steps.

Observed logs / headers (example):
- x-rate-limit-limit: 1000
- x-rate-limit-remaining: 0
- x-rate-limit-reset: 24
- x-rate-limit-window: 15s
- ingress-proxy logs show a spike in POSTs to /warmup from signed-url agents at t=00:02:10 and again t=00:02:35 etc.

Workaround tried by customer:
- Increased client-side jitter between warmup workers (reduced magnitude, not eliminate).
- Staggered warmup start times (reduces synchronization but not fully effective because refill epochs remain aligned).

Requested from Support:
- Explain why 429s are rhythmic rather than random.
- Identify configuration changes (tenant burst window, refill smoothing) or recommended warmup patterns to avoid periodic throttling.

Next steps: reproduce in a controlled dedicated-pool staging of Nimbus Labs and review token-bucket refill timing and proxy preflight accounting.
comments: 2026-03-10 12:08 - Aisha Patel: Initial triage - customer reports exact spike cadence (~20-25s). Asked for recent request timeline and warmup job config.
2026-03-10 12:34 - Nimbus Labs (support contact Mira Chen): Attached warmup job logs and sample headers; confirmed changing jitter slightly reduces but does not remove spikes.
2026-03-10 14:12 - Marco Alvarez (SRE): Noted similarity to refill-window-alignment phenomena. Will instrument refill events and token-bucket state on the tenant's ingress nodes.

2026-03-11 09:05 - Marco Alvarez: Added quick metric dashboard link to tenant token bucket counters and ingress proxy request heatmap (internal). Requested permission to run synthetic warmups against a staging replica.

2026-03-12 16:20 - Product Ops (Elena Rossi): Suggest short-term mitigation: increase tenant burst window to 30s for the scheduled warmup time window and add small randomized refill jitter. Confirming change scheduled during low-traffic window.
2026-03-12 18:01 - Nimbus Labs (Mira Chen): Requested that mitigation be applied only to their dedicated pool and asked if there is any billing impact for increased burst allowance.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Token-bucket refill epochs across the ingress fleet are synchronized; when warmup clients align with refill boundary, remaining tokens drop to zero simultaneously causing the sawtooth 429 pattern.
Hypothesis 2: Dedicated autoscaler shifts (scale-up events) cause short-lived route weight movements which temporarily increase token accounting on origin, amplifying the refill alignment effect.
Hypothesis 3: Health-check or warmup preflight probes from signed-url workers are counted against the tenant bucket and are batched at scheduler intervals, contributing to periodic token drains.

Data collected: Ingress token-bucket counters capture shows ~7 refill events/minute with high variance but clear periodicity matching customer timeline. Proxy logs show fanout of 18 warmup workers initiating within 200ms of each other at warmup start times.

Reproduction attempt: Running synthetic warmup in staging with 20 concurrent workers recreated sawtooth 429s when refill jitter disabled. Introducing per-ingress refill jitter removed strong periodicity in staging.
Related: linked to SUP-762318 (nightly billing sweep refill anomaly) because both involve epoch/refill alignment, but different root cause (nightly sweep vs customer warmup job).
resolution_notes: Mitigation applied 2026-03-12 22:00: temporary tenant-level config: burst_window set to 30s for Nimbus Labs dedicated pool during scheduled warmup window (00:00-01:00 UTC). Per-ingress refill jitter (±300ms) enabled globally behind a feature flag to smooth refill epochs. Customer confirmed initial night after mitigation showed >90% reduction in 429 spike magnitude and no change to daily billing tier. Next steps: schedule follow-up to make jitter default and evaluate long-term smoothing algorithm in rate-limiter (engineering RFC).
final_resolution_status: Mitigation deployed; long-term fix planned (rate-limiter smoothing RFC)
customer_impact_summary: Dedicated customer warmup job experienced periodic 429 bursts impacting background throughput and causing retries; mitigation reduced spike severity and restored steady throughput during warmup.
follow_up_actions: Engineering: RFC for rate-limiter refill smoothing and tenant-aware burst heuristics (assigned to runtime team)
SRE: Monitor tenant token-bucket counter heatmaps for next 7 days and confirm no regression (dashboard shared)
Support: Document warmup best-practices for customers (stagger, introduce client jitter, avoid large concurrent short-lived workers at exact epoch boundaries)
Billing: Confirm no cost changes for temporary burst window increase (finance notified)
Customer Success: Schedule 1:1 with Nimbus Labs to review warmup pattern and possible scheduled warmup orchestration improvements
